'''Valtteri Viktor Bottas''' ({{IPA|fi|ˈʋɑltːeri ˈbotːɑs}}; born 28 August 1989) is a Finnish [[racing driver]] who competes in [[Formula One]] for [[Cadillac in Formula One|Cadillac]]. Bottas has twice finished runner-up in the [[World Drivers' Championship]] in {{F1|2019}} and {{F1|2020}} with Mercedes, and has won 10 [[Formula One Grands Prix|Grands Prix]] across 13 seasons.

Born and raised in [[Nastola]], Bottas began [[kart racing]] aged six. After studying [[automotive engineering]] and completing [[Conscription in Finland|mandatory military service]], Bottas progressed to [[junior formulae]] in 2007. He won his first championship at the [[Formula Renault NEC]] in [[2008 Formula Renault 2.0 Northern European Cup|2008]], also winning the [[2008 Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0|Formula Renault Eurocup]] by three points to [[Daniel Ricciardo]], both with [[Motopark]]. He then won the [[Masters of Formula 3]] back-to-back in [[2009 Masters of Formula 3|2009]] and [[2010 Masters of Formula 3|2010]] with [[ART Grand Prix|ART]], before winning the [[GP3 Series]] in [[2011 GP3 Series|2011]]. After two years as a test driver, Bottas signed for [[Williams Racing|Williams]] in {{F1|2013}} to partner [[Pastor Maldonado]], making his Formula One debut at the {{F1GP|2013|Australian}}. In {{F1|2014}}, he finished fourth in the championship, taking his maiden career podium at the {{F1GP|2014|Austrian}}. Across four seasons at Williams, Bottas finished on the podium nine times.

Bottas signed for [[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]] in {{F1|2017}}, replacing the retiring [[Nico Rosberg]] to partner [[Lewis Hamilton]]. He took his maiden [[List of Formula One polesitters|pole position]] in [[2017 Bahrain Grand Prix|Bahrain]] and his maiden [[List of Formula One Grand Prix winners|win]] in [[2017 Russian Grand Prix|Russia]], finishing third in the championship following further victories in [[2017 Austrian Grand Prix|Austria]] and [[2017 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix|Abu Dhabi]]. After a winless {{F1|2018}} campaign, Bottas finished runner-up to Hamilton in both the {{F1|2019}} and {{F1|2020}} seasons. He took his final win for Mercedes at the {{F1GP|2021|Turkish}} in {{F1|2021}}, leaving at the end of the season after contributing to five consecutive [[World Constructors' Championship]]s. He joined [[Alfa Romeo in Formula One|Alfa Romeo]] in {{F1|2022}}, retaining his seat for his {{F1|2023}} campaign. After a non-scoring {{F1|2024}} season at the re-branded [[Sauber]], Bottas returned to Mercedes as a [[reserve driver]]. He became a full-time driver again for the [[2026 Formula One World Championship|2026 season]], driving for Cadillac.

Bottas has achieved {{F1stat|BOT|wins}} race wins, {{F1stat|BOT|poles}} pole positions, {{F1stat|BOT|fastestlaps}} fastest laps and {{F1stat|BOT|podiums}} podiums in Formula One. He is the driver with the [[List of Formula One driver records#Most career points without being World Champion|second most career points without a World Drivers' Championship]] ({{Commas|{{F1stat|BOT|careerpoints}}}}).

== Early life ==

Tee supervaikea testi ja selvitä paikkasi varikolla! |date=28 January 2021 |access-date=25 March 2024 |language=fi}}</ref> He completed [[Conscription in Finland|mandatory]] military service in the {{Interlanguage link|Finnish Defence Forces Sports School|fi|Puolustusvoimien urheilukoulu}} in [[Lahti]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=8 January 2020 |title=Valtteri Bottas piipahti koulussa kertomassa F3- kuninkuushaaveista |trans-title=Valtteri Bottas visits school to talk on dreams of F3 kingship |url=https://www.ess.fi/urheilu/389322 |access-date=25 March 2024 |work=[[Etelä-Suomen Sanomat]] |language=fi |issn=0359-5056}}</ref> His military rank is [[Lance corporal#Finland|lance corporal]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Muut |date=12 November 2014 |title=Bottas olisi valmis vaikka heti F1-kisoihin |trans-title=Bottas would be ready for F1 races right away |url=http://www.ts.fi/moottoriurheilu/muut/147323/Bottas+olisi+valmis+vaikka+heti+F1kisoihin |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112010625/http://www.ts.fi/moottoriurheilu/muut/147323/Bottas+olisi+valmis+vaikka+heti+F1kisoihin |archive-date=12 November 2014 |access-date=27 April 2017 |website=[[Turun Sanomat]] |language=fi}}</ref>

==Junior racing career==

===Karting===
Bottas's interest in [[motorsport]] was sparked at the age of six by a chance visit to a [[Kart racing|karting]] event that he had seen advertised at his local supermarket while shopping with his grandfather.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Valtteri Bottas on mental resilience, motivation and the power of porridge {{!}} Formula 1®|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.valtteri-bottas-on-mental-resilience-motivation-and-the-power-of-porridge.29ra0UP648maClasR5vcHg.html|access-date=10 September 2021|website=Formula1 |language=en}}</ref> His racing hero while growing up was compatriot [[Mika Häkkinen]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Formula 1|url=https://f1tv.formula1.com/|access-date=10 September 2021|website=F1 TV|language=en}}</ref>

Bottas finished eighth in the 2005 Karting World Cup for the P.D.B. Racing Team, using a [[Gillard (kart manufacturer)|Gillard]] chassis and Parilla engines.{{citation needed|date=December 2025}}

===Lower formulae===
Bottas won both the [[2008 Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0 season|2008 Formula Renault Eurocup]] and the [[2008 Formula Renault seasons#Formula Renault 2.0 Northern European Cup season|2008 Formula Renault Northern European Cup]]. In doing so, he repeated the feat of [[Filipe Albuquerque]], who won both the NEC and Eurocup in the same season, in 2006.

Bottas would have also won the 2007 [[British Formula Renault Championship|Formula Renault UK Winter Series]], had he been holding an [[Motor Sports Association|MSA]]-registered licence for the championship. This did not stop him from competing, and he won three out of the four races in the championship.

[[File:Formel3 Mercedes Bottas 2010 amk.jpg|thumb|left|Bottas competing at the second round of the [[2010 Formula 3 Euro Series]] at [[Hockenheimring|Hockenheim]]]]

=== Formula Three ===
Bottas moved up into the [[Formula 3 Euro Series|Formula Three Euroseries]] for the [[2009 Formula 3 Euro Series|2009 season]], competing for reigning champions [[ART Grand Prix]]. Despite not winning a race, Bottas set two pole positions on his way to third in the championship, edging out future [[BMW|BMW i]] [[Andretti Autosport|Andretti Motorsport]] driver [[Alexander Sims (racing driver)|Alexander Sims]] at the final race. In June 2009, Bottas won the [[2009 Masters of Formula 3|2009]] [[Masters of Formula 3]], also claiming the pole position and setting the fastest lap of the race. By winning the event again in [[2010 Masters of Formula 3|2010]], he became the first driver to win the F3 Masters title for the second time.<ref>{{cite web | title=Bottas makes history at Zandvoort Masters | work=Motorsport.com | url=http://www.motorsport.com/news/article.asp?ID=371703&FS= | date=6 June 2010 | access-date=6 June 2010}}</ref>

In 2011, Bottas contested the [[GP3 Series]], remaining with F3 squad ART.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bottas lands Lotus ART seat for 2011 |work=MotorsTV.com |url=http://www.motorstv.com/car/single-seater/gp3-series/23112010/gp3-bottas-lands-lotus-art-seat-2011 |date=23 November 2010 |access-date=23 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305022715/http://www.motorstv.com/car/single-seater/gp3-series/23112010/gp3-bottas-lands-lotus-art-seat-2011 |archive-date=5 March 2012 }}</ref> After a tough start to the season, he claimed a win in each of the last four race weekends and secured the title by winning the penultimate race ahead of his teammate and future [[Jaguar Racing]] driver [[James Calado]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Champion win for Bottas in Monza |work=GP3 Series |url=http://www.gp3series.com/news/Monza-Rd-8-2011/Bottas-wins-to-take-crown/ |date=10 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926020729/http://www.gp3series.com/news/Monza-Rd-8-2011/Bottas-wins-to-take-crown/ |archive-date=26 September 2011 }}</ref>

==Formula One career==
===Williams (2010–2016)===
====2010–2012: Test and reserve driver====
[[File:Valtteri Bottas 2012 Malaysia FP1 1.jpg|thumb|right|Bottas making his Grand Prix weekend debut at the [[2012 Malaysian Grand Prix]]]]
Bottas was signed as the official [[Formula One]] test driver for the [[Williams F1|Williams]] team in January 2010 after his first year in the [[Formula 3 Euro Series]]. Team principal [[Frank Williams (Formula One)|Frank Williams]] praised Bottas's record in the junior categories and expressed his hope that the role would "provide him with another step in his development".<ref>{{cite news|title=Williams signs Bottas as test driver|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/81111|first=Matt|last=Beer|work=autosport.com|publisher=[[Haymarket Group|Haymarket Publications]]|date=29 January 2010|access-date=29 January 2010}}</ref> He conducted straight-line aerodynamic testing in the team's [[Williams FW32|FW32]] during the year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.auto123.com/en/news/f3-valtteri-bottas-accepts-williams-abu-dhabi-test-axe/7810/|title=F3: Valtteri Bottas accepts Williams' Abu Dhabi test axe|website=auto123.com|first=Khatir|last=Soltani|date=27 October 2010|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref> He continued in the role for 2011 and took part in his first full test in November, driving the [[Williams FW33|FW33]] in the post-season young drivers' test at [[Yas Marina Circuit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecheckeredflag.co.uk/2011/11/abu-dhabi-young-driver-test-day-1-quotes-bottas-williams/|title=Abu Dhabi Young Driver Test Day 1 Quotes: Bottas & Williams|website=thecheckeredflag.co.uk|first=David|last=Bean|date=15 November 2011|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref> His role was expanded in 2012 after his GP3 Series victory; he took part in fifteen Friday practice sessions, making his Grand Prix weekend debut at the {{F1 GP|2012|Malaysian}}.

====2013: Debut season====
[[File:Valtteri Bottas 2013 Malaysia FP1.jpg|thumb|Bottas during practice at the [[2013 Malaysian Grand Prix]]]]
In November 2012, it was announced that Bottas would replace [[Bruno Senna]] and partner [[Pastor Maldonado]] as a full-time Williams race driver for the {{F1|2013}} season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Elizalde|first=Pablo|title=Williams confirms Valtteri Bottas and Pastor Maldonado for 2013|publisher=[[Haymarket Group|Haymarket Publications]]|work=autosport.com|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/104630|date=28 November 2012|access-date=28 November 2012}}</ref> He qualified 16th, ahead of Maldonado, and finished 14th at his debut race, the {{F1 GP|2013|Australian}}. He improved from 18th on the grid to 11th at the finish at the {{F1 GP|2013|Malaysian}}, 1.5 seconds behind a points-paying position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.f1technical.net/news/18279|title=Bottas misses first F1 point by 1.5 seconds|website=f1technical.net|first=Steven|last=de Groote|date=24 March 2013|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref> He qualified third at the {{F1 GP|2013|Canadian}} behind [[Sebastian Vettel]] and [[Lewis Hamilton]], the first time a Williams car had qualified in the top ten that year.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/107950|title=Canadian GP: Vettel claims pole in rain-hit session|last=Beer|first=Matt|date=8 June 2013|work=Autosport.com|publisher=Haymarket|access-date=8 June 2013}}</ref> He was unable to hold the position in the race and dropped to 14th at the finish line. He later stated that "the car pace was just not there" and that he believed the result would have been the same regardless of the team's strategy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/valtteri-bottas-says-canadian-grand-prix-slump-was-inevitable-4467309/4467309/|title=Valtteri Bottas says Canadian Grand Prix slump was inevitable|website=autosport.com|first1=Edd|last1=Straw|first2=Matt|last2=Beer|date=10 June 2013|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref> A hydraulics failure at the {{F1 GP|2013|Hungarian}} caused his first retirement of the season whilst Maldonado finished tenth to claim the team's first point of 2013. Bottas qualified ninth and finished eighth at the {{F1 GP|2013|United States}}, his first Formula One points and the team's best result of the season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1852260-united-states-f1-grand-prix-2013-results-times-for-practice-and-qualifying|work=Bleacher Report|date=16 November 2013|access-date=19 May 2023|last=Patterson|first=Mark|title=United States F1 Grand Prix 2013: Results, Times for Practice and Qualifying}}</ref> He collided with Hamilton whilst unlapping himself at the season-ending {{F1 GP|2013|Brazilian}}, later stating he was unaware Hamilton was a lap ahead.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ESPN Staff |date=24 November 2013 |title=Bottas unaware he wasn't racing Hamilton |url=http://en.espn.co.uk/brazil/motorsport/story/137519.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240410130603/http://en.espn.co.uk/brazil/motorsport/story/137519.html |archive-date=10 April 2024 |access-date=10 April 2024 |website=[[ESPN (UK)]]}}</ref>

Bottas ended his debut season 17th in the World Drivers' Championship, scoring four of Williams's five points.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2013/drivers.html|title=2013 Driver Standings|work=Formula 1|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref> He qualified ahead of Maldonado at twelve of the nineteen races and was praised for his performances at the Canadian and United States Grands Prix.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.racefans.net/2013/12/14/2013-f1-season-driver-rankings-part-two-10/|title=2013 F1 season driver rankings part two: 16-11|website=racefans.net|first=Keith|last=Collantine|date=14 December 2013|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/22058/9043359/driver-by-driver-2013-season-review|title=Driver-by-driver 2013 season review|website=skysports.com|first=James|last=Galloway|date=28 November 2013|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref>

====2014: First podiums====
[[File:Valtteri Bottas 2014 Singapore FP2.jpg|thumbnail|Bottas at the [[2014 Singapore Grand Prix]]|left]]
Bottas was retained by Williams for the {{F1|2014}} season, partnering [[Felipe Massa]] who was signed from [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/24897809|title=Felipe Massa joins Williams for 2014 to replace Pastor Maldonado|last=Benson|first=Andrew|date=11 November 2013|work=bbc.co.uk|publisher=BBC|access-date=11 November 2013}}</ref> At the season-opening {{F1 GP|2014|Australian}}, Bottas started fifteenth due to a gearbox change penalty<ref>{{cite report|title=FIA Stewards Decision — Document No. 38|url=http://184.106.145.74/f1-championship/f1-2014/f1-2014-01/Formula%20One%20Australian%20Grand%20Prix%202014%20Document%20-%2038.pdf|work=FIA.com|publisher=[[Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile]]|date=15 March 2014|access-date=19 June 2014|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140318102936/http://184.106.145.74/f1-championship/f1-2014/f1-2014-01/Formula%20One%20Australian%20Grand%20Prix%202014%20Document%20-%2038.pdf|archive-date = 18 March 2014|url-status = dead}}</ref> and clipped the wall causing a tyre puncture in the race, but recovered to sixth at the finish and was later promoted to fifth after [[Daniel Ricciardo]]'s disqualification.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2014/mar/16/daniel-ricciardo-stewards-decision-second-place-f1|title=Daniel Ricciardo disqualified from Australia GP|date=16 March 2014|access-date=16 March 2014|work=[[The Guardian]]|first=Paul|last=Weaver}}</ref> He received another grid penalty and started 18th at the next race, the {{F1 GP|2014|Malaysian}}, for impeding Ricciardo in qualifying, but gained places to finish eighth. He matched his best grid position at the {{F1 GP|2014|Bahrain}}, starting third, but dropped to eighth at the finish. He praised the team's updates to his [[Williams FW36|FW36]] after finishing fifth at the {{F1 GP|2024|Spanish}} and felt that the team now had the third-fastest car,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12476/9308367/valtteri-bottas-feels-williams-now-have-the-third-quickest-car-after-spanish-updates|title=Valtteri Bottas feels Williams now have the third quickest car after Spanish updates|website=skysports.com|first=William|last=Esler|date=12 May 2014|accessdate=10 April 2024}}</ref> however this was followed by 13th place in qualifying and an engine failure at the {{F1 GP|2014|Monaco}}.

====2016====
[[File:Valtteri Bottas 2016 Malaysia FP2.jpg|thumb|right|Bottas at the [[2016 Malaysian Grand Prix]]]]
Bottas and Massa remained teammates at Williams for the {{F1|2016}} season. A gearbox penalty required him to start the season-opening {{F1 GP|2016|Australian}} from 16th place, but he recovered to score points in the race. He was judged to have caused a lap-one collision with Lewis Hamilton at the {{F1 GP|2016|Bahrain}} and received a drive-through penalty; he started sixth and finished ninth. He scored more points at the following three races and achieved his best qualifying performance of the season at the {{F1 GP|2016|Russian}}, starting third and finishing fourth. This made Bottas and Massa the only two drivers to score points in each of the first five races of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stat Wrap: 2016 Spanish Grand Prix |work=Channel 4 |url=http://f1.channel4.com/news/stat-wrap-2016-spanish-grand-prix/ |date=16 May 2016}}</ref> This streak ended at the {{F1 GP|2016|Monaco}}, where Bottas started and finished 11th but was demoted to 12th for causing a collision with [[Esteban Gutiérrez]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stewards Decision Doc47 – V.Bottas|url=http://www.fia.com/file/42557/download?token=-qs4iR0r|publisher=[[Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile|FIA]]|access-date=3 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603155225/http://www.fia.com/file/42557/download?token=-qs4iR0r|archive-date=3 June 2016|date=29 May 2016}}</ref> He claimed the team's only podium finish of 2016 at the {{F1 GP|2016|Canadian}}; he qualified seventh but executed a one-stop strategy and climbed to third at the finish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2645470-canadian-grand-prix-2016-winners-and-losers-from-montreal-race|title=Canadian Grand Prix 2016: Winners and Losers from Montreal Race|website=bleacherreport.com|first=Oliver|last=Harden|date=13 June 2016|accessdate=11 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Bottas lauds 'perfect' Williams strategy after Canada podium |work=ESPN |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/16157503/bottas-lauds-perfect-williams-strategy-canada-podium|date=12 June 2016|last=Saunders|first=Nate|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref>

Bottas achieved an unofficial Formula One record speed of {{convert|378|kph|mph|abbr=on}} at the [[Baku City Circuit]] during qualifying for the {{F1 GP|2016|European}}.<ref name="stats">{{cite web|last1=Collantine|first1=Keith|title=Williams hit record speeds on and off the track|url=http://www.f1fanatic.co.uk/2016/06/20/2016-european-grand-prix-stats-and-facts/|publisher=F1Fanatic|access-date=20 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160620134711/http://www.f1fanatic.co.uk/2016/06/20/2016-european-grand-prix-stats-and-facts/|archive-date=20 June 2016|date=20 June 2016}}</ref> He started sixth at the {{F1 GP|2016|British}} but a spin dropped him outside the points. He scored points at the following four races, including sixth place at the {{F1 GP|2016|Italian}}, but retired from the {{F1 GP|2016|Singapore}} after picking up a puncture and encountering issues with his seatbelt and gearbox.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/bottas-seatbelt-issues-in-singapore-gp-a-worry-for-williams-f1-team-5034601/5034601/|title=Bottas seatbelt issues in Singapore GP a worry for Williams F1 team|website=autosport.com|first1=Ian|last1=Parkes|first2=Stuart|last2=Codling|date=20 September 2016|accessdate=11 April 2024}}</ref> This was followed by a drive from 11th on the grid to fifth place at the {{F1 GP|2016|Malaysian}}. A first lap puncture caused him to fall outside the points after qualifying eighth at the {{F1 GP|2016|United States}}, and his season ended with a suspension-related retirement at the {{F1 GP|2016|Abu Dhabi}}.

Bottas finished the season eighth in the World Drivers' Championship, scoring 85 points to Massa's 53 and qualifying ahead of his teammate at seventeen of the twenty-one races.<ref>{{cite web|title=2016 F1 season driver rankings #10: Bottas |work=racefans.net |url=https://www.racefans.net/2016/12/12/2016-f1-season-driver-rankings-10-bottas/ |date=12 December 2016}}</ref> Williams finished fifth in the World Constructors' Championship, down from third in the previous two years.

Bottas qualified sixth at the {{F1 GP|2017|Singapore}} and gained from strategy and the four-car collision on the first lap to finish third.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2733634-lewis-hamilton-wins-crash-filled-2017-singapore-f1-grand-prix-extends-lead|title=Lewis Hamilton Wins Crash-Filled 2017 Singapore F1 Grand Prix, Extends Lead|work=Bleacher Report|last=Marsden|first=Rory|date=17 September 2017|access-date=23 May 2023}}</ref> He finished off the podium for the next three races while Hamilton claimed two wins and a second place, but his performances helped Mercedes clinch their fourth consecutive Constructors' Championship at the {{F1 GP|2017|United States}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/motorsport/formula-one/live-2017-formula-1-united-states-grand-prix/news-story/921264a87131b73a88e2ff47b8794a9d|work=Fox Sports|agency=Agence France-Presse|date=23 October 2017|access-date=23 May 2023|title=Lewis Hamilton wins United States Grand Prix, Mercedes secures Constructors' Championship|via=Fox Sports Australia}}</ref> He returned to the podium at the {{F1 GP|2017|Mexican}}, starting fourth but benefiting from contact between Vettel and Hamilton to finish second. His third pole position of the season came at the {{F1 GP|2017|Brazilian}}, but he again finished second after losing the lead to Vettel at the first corner.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/nov/12/sebastian-vettel-f1-brazilian-grand-prix-lewis-hamilton-race-report|work=The Guardian|date=12 November 2017|access-date=23 May 2023|last=Richards|first=Giles|title=Sebastian Vettel wins Brazilian Grand Prix after Lewis Hamilton fightback}}</ref> He claimed pole position again at the season-ending {{F1 GP|2017|Abu Dhabi}} and went on to achieve his third Grand Prix victory.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/f1/2017/11/26/16701364/2017-f1-abu-dhabi-grand-prix-winner-results-finishing-order|title=F1 results 2017: Valtteri Bottas wins Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, plus full finishing order|last=Brady|first=James|work=SB Nation|date=26 November 2017|access-date=23 May 2023}}</ref>

Bottas finished third overall in the World Drivers' Championship with 305 points, compared to 363 for teammate and champion Hamilton,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2017/drivers.html|title=2017 Driver Standings|work=Formula 1|access-date=23 May 2023}}</ref> and qualified ahead of Hamilton at six of the nineteen races.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.racefans.net/2017/12/15/2017-f1-driver-rankings-6-bottas/|title=2017 F1 driver rankings #6: Bottas|website=racefans.net|first=Keith|last=Collantine|date=15 December 2017|accessdate=12 April 2017}}</ref> He was praised for his performances early in the season, but [[Martin Brundle]] commented that he "went on the missing list after August"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/11116386/formula-1-2017-rating-the-drivers|title=Formula 1 2017: Rating the drivers|website=skysports.com|date=29 November 2017|accessdate=12 April 2024}}</ref> and Bottas described his own season as "disappointing".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/21585168/valtteri-bottas-rates-2017-disappointing-abu-dhabi-win|title=Valtteri Bottas rates 2017 'disappointing' despite Abu Dhabi win|website=espn.co.uk|first=Lewis|last=Larkam|date=27 November 2017|accessdate=12 April 2017}}</ref>

====2018: Underwhelming season====
[[File:Valtteri Bottas-Test Days Circuit Barcelona (3).jpg|thumb|Bottas testing for Mercedes in 2018|right]]

In September 2017, Mercedes announced that Bottas would remain with the team for the {{F1|2018}} season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Silver Arrows and Valtteri Bottas together in 2018|url=https://www.mercedesamgf1.com/en/mercedes-amg-f1/silver-arrows-and-valtteri-bottas-together-in-2018|website=Mercedes F1 team|access-date=13 September 2017|archive-date=4 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201004133443/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.breaking-valtteri-bottas-signs-new-deal-to-drive-for-mercedes-in-2021.5kdl5Krly4Y3Z1l6dCVJjy.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He started 15th at the season-opening {{F1 GP|2018|Australian}} after crashing in qualifying and taking a gearbox penalty,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/motorsport/formula-one/f1-valtteri-bottas-hit-with-grid-penalty-after-australian-gp-qualifying-crash/news-story/449694151e28392501f75a27d91637ec|work=News Corp Australia|via=Fox Sports Australia|date=25 March 2018|access-date=26 May 2023|last=Dale|first=Will|title=F1: Valtteri Bottas hit with grid penalty after Australian GP qualifying crash}}</ref> but recovered to score points in eighth place.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/mar/25/australian-grand-prix-sebastian-vettel-wins-f1-2018-season-opener|date=25 March 2018|access-date=26 May 2023|last=Richards|first=Giles|location=Albert Park, Melbourne|title=Australian Grand Prix: Sebastian Vettel wins F1 opener with Lewis Hamilton second|work=The Guardian}}</ref> He qualified third, ahead of Hamilton, at the {{F1 GP|2018|Bahrain}}. He overtook Räikkönen at the start and finished less than a second behind race winner Vettel.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/formula1/43683493|work=BBC Sport|last=Benson|first=Andrew|location=Sakhir, Bahrain|date=8 April 2018|access-date=26 May 2023|title=Bahrain GP: Sebastian Vettel wins, Lewis Hamilton third after fine overtake}}</ref> He again qualified third ahead of Hamilton at the {{F1 GP|2018|Chinese}} and overtook both Ferraris to lead the race, but was ultimately passed by Daniel Ricciardo, who used a safety car period to pit for fresh tyres.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/apr/15/daniel-ricciardo-claims-chinese-grand-prix-as-verstappen-clips-vettel|work=The Guardian|last=Richards|first=Giles|title=Daniel Ricciardo wins Chinese Grand Prix as Verstappen clips Vettel|date=15 April 2018|access-date=27 May 2023}}</ref> He was leading the {{F1 GP|2018|Azerbaijan}} with two laps remaining but ran over a piece of debris, causing a puncture and forcing him into retirement.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-debris-cost-baku-win-1031739/3068738/|work=Motorsport.com|title=Bottas didn't see debris that cost him Baku win|date=29 April 2018|access-date=27 May 2023}}</ref> Further podiums came with second-place finishes at the [[2018 Spanish Grand Prix|Spanish]] and [[2018 Canadian Grand Prix|Canadian]] Grands Prix.

Bottas qualified second at the {{F1 GP|2018|French}} but was hit by Vettel at the start, requiring him to pit for repairs and resulting in a seventh-place finish. Vettel accepted responsibility for the collision,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/vettel-shoulders-blame-for-bottas-crash.IdAra66GI02U6AkC4o6oW|title=Vettel shoulders blame for Bottas crash|website=formula1.com|date=24 June 2018|accessdate=12 April 2024}}</ref> and Bottas remarked that the race "sums up my season so far".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://readmotorsport.com/2018/06/24/bottas-disappointing-french-gp-sums-up-my-season/|title=Bottas: Disappointing French GP 'sums up my season'|website=readmotorsport.com|first=Hamilton|last=Lyndon-Griffiths|date=24 June 2018 |accessdate=12 April 2024}}</ref> He took his first pole position of the year at the {{F1 GP|2018|Austrian}} but lost the lead to Hamilton on the first lap and then retired with a gearbox failure. He challenged Hamilton for the lead at the {{F1 GP|2018|German}} but was ordered by Mercedes to "hold position" and finish second.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hamilton retakes title lead as Vettel crashes out |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/formula1/44912617 |access-date=28 January 2023}}</ref> He was running in second place in the closing laps of the {{F1 GP|2018|Hungarian}}, but dropped to fifth after making contact with Vettel and Ricciardo in separate incidents. Mercedes team principal [[Toto Wolff]] praised Bottas's defence against the Ferraris and described him as a "sensational [[Wingman (social)|wingman]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Noble |first=Jonathan |date=29 July 2018 |title=Bottas "hurt" by Wolff's "wingman" comments |url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-hurt-by-wolff-s-wingman-comments-1065731/3150676/ |access-date=30 July 2022 |website=Motorsport.com}}</ref> Bottas commented that the description was hurtful and that he would discuss the situation with team management.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Ben |date=29 July 2018 |title=Wolff clarifies Bottas "wingman" comment |url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/wolff-clarifies-wingman-comments-bottas-1065789/3150780/ |access-date=30 July 2022 |website=Motorsport.com}}</ref> He started 17th at the {{F1 GP|2018|Belgian}} due to a power unit components penalty but recovered to fourth place in the race.

Bottas was promoted to the podium at the {{F1 GP|2018|Italian}} after Max Verstappen received a penalty for colliding with him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2018/races/992/italy/race-result.html |title=Formula 1 Gran Premio Heineken d'Italia 2018 – Race Result |website=Formula1.com |publisher=Formula One World Championship Limited |date=2 September 2018 |access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref> He claimed pole position at the {{F1 GP|2018|Russian}} but was ordered by Mercedes to concede his position to Hamilton during the race. Hamilton later indicated that he was unhappy with the order, but Wolff remarked that maximising Hamilton's championship points was the "harsh reality", with Bottas commenting "Lewis is fighting for the drivers' championship and I'm not".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/sep/30/lewis-hamilton-wins-russian-grand-prix-mercedes-team-orders-sebastian-vettel|title=Lewis Hamilton wins Russian Grand Prix but is unhappy with team orders|last=Richards|first=Giles|date=30 September 2018|work=The Guardian|access-date=11 January 2019|issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.opinion-why-mercedes-used-team-orders-and-why-they-were-right-to-do-so.1VZaX1iWz284gcGia6mmC6.html|title=Opinion: Why Mercedes used team orders – and why they were right to do so|website=Formula1.com|access-date=11 January 2019}}</ref> The {{F1 GP|2018|Japanese}} was his eighth and final podium finish of the year, and he finished fifth at each of the remaining four races.

Bottas became the first Mercedes driver to finish a season without a win since [[Michael Schumacher]] in 2012, and set a record for the most second-place finishes (seven) in a season without a win.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hamilton signs off title-winning campaign with dominant Abu Dhabi victory |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.hamilton-signs-off-championship-winning-campaign-with-dominant-abu-dhabi-win.2G7UhAGiVOMQkmooauiI4Y.html |access-date=25 November 2018 |publisher=Formula1.com |date=25 November 2018}}</ref> He finished fifth overall in the World Drivers' Championship with 247 points, whilst teammate Hamilton won his fifth world title with 408 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2018/drivers.html|work=Formula 1|access-date=27 May 2023|title=2018 Driver Standings}}</ref> He described 2018 as his worst season in Formula One,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/valtteri-bottas-2018-my-worst-season-in-formula-1-5285902/5285902/|title=Valtteri Bottas: 2018 my worst season in Formula 1|website=autosport.com|first=Jonathan|last=Noble|date=2 December 2018|accessdate=12 April 2024}}</ref> and later revealed that he almost retired from the sport at the end of the season, stating "I lost the joy of F1".<ref name="2018interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/34129966/valtteri-bottas-nearly-quit-f1-2018|title=Valtteri Bottas nearly quit F1 after 2018 championship challenge with Lewis Hamilton|website=espn.co.uk|first=Nate|last=Saunders|date=22 June 2022|accessdate=12 April 2024}}</ref>

====2019–2020: Championship runner-up====
[[File:F1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix 2019 podium.jpg|thumb|right|Bottas on the podium after winning the [[2019 Azerbaijan Grand Prix]]]]
In July 2018, Bottas signed a contract extension with Mercedes for the {{F1|2019}} season with an option for 2020, continuing alongside Hamilton.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/27993/11441817/valtteri-bottas-now-signed-up-to-mercedes-for-f1-2019|title=Valtteri Bottas now signed up to Mercedes for F1 2019|website=skysports.com|first1=Pete|last1=Gill|first2=James|last2=Galloway|date=20 July 2018|accessdate=13 April 2024}}</ref> He qualified second behind Hamilton at the {{F1 GP|2019|Australian}} but overtook Hamilton at the first corner. Bottas went on to win the race by over 20 seconds ahead of Hamilton, his fourth Grand Prix victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/mar/17/valtteri-bottas-leads-from-first-turn-to-win-australian-grand-prix |title =Valtteri Bottas dominates Australian Grand Prix to win Formula One opener|date=17 March 2019|work=Guardian|access-date=20 March 2019}}</ref> After crossing the finish line, he exclaimed over the radio "to whom it may concern, fuck you", which he later explained was aimed at both himself and the critics of his 2018 performance.<ref name="2018interview"/> He finished second behind Hamilton at the {{F1 GP|2019|Bahrain}} after race leader [[Charles Leclerc]] slowed with engine issues and dropped behind the Mercedes drivers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.report-bahrain-grand-prix-2019-hamilton-leclerc.XaZcYj1U3innMvc5zJZqK.html|work=Formula 1|access-date=27 May 2023|date=31 March 2019|title=Hamilton profits from Leclerc reliability woe to win in Bahrain}}</ref> He took pole position at the {{F1 GP|2019|Chinese}} but lost the position to Hamilton at the start, who led the entire race distance to win.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/chinese-gp-race-hamilton-bottas/4370435/|title=Chinese GP: Hamilton leads third consecutive Mercedes 1-2|work=Motorsport.com|last=Codling|first=Stuart|date=14 April 2019|access-date=27 May 2023}}</ref> Bottas followed this with a victory from pole at the {{F1 GP|2019|Azerbaijan}}, promoting him to the lead of the championship by one point over Hamilton.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/apr/28/valtteri-bottas-wins-azerbaijan-grand-prix-lewis-hamilton|title =Valtteri Bottas wins Azerbaijan Grand Prix with Lewis Hamilton second|date=28 April 2019|work=Guardian|access-date=30 April 2019}}</ref>

[[File:FIA F1 Austria 2019 Nr. 77 Bottas 1.jpg|thumb|left|Bottas at the [[2019 Austrian Grand Prix]]]]
Azerbaijan would be the final time that Bottas led the championship as Hamilton would win the next four races. Bottas took his third consecutive pole at the {{F1 GP|2019|Spanish}} but was overtaken by Hamilton at the first corner and finished second, achieving Mercedes' fifth one-two finish in a row.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/motorsport/formula-one/f1-spanish-grand-prix-2019-five-things-we-learned/news-story/5717bb9876055b269db5b33c419a4537|title=F1 news, Spanish Grand Prix 2019: Ferrari in crisis as Renault upgrade fail Daniel Ricciardo - Five things we learned|work=Fox Sports Australia|date=13 May 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|last=Austin|first=Jack}}</ref> He qualified second at the {{F1 GP|2019|Monaco}} but finished third behind Sebastian Vettel after making contact with Max Verstappen in the pit lane.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2019/drivers.html|title=2019 Driver Standings|work=Formula 1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526191916/https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2019/drivers.html|archive-date=26 May 2019|access-date=31 May 2019}}</ref> He qualified sixth and finished off the podium at the {{F1 GP|2019|Canadian}} and placed second behind Hamilton at the {{F1 GP|2019|French}}. He finished third at the {{F1 GP|2019|Austrian}}, ahead of Hamilton for the first time since Azerbaijan, but failed to convert pole position into victory at the {{F1 GP|2019|British}} after Hamilton took advantage of a safety car to jump ahead of Bottas in the pit stop phase.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Brilliant Bottas beats Hamilton to British GP pole by just 0.006s|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.British-grand-prix-2019-qualifying-report-highlights.1QM7IStT79XC6iRfB2rM2l.html|work=Formula 1|date=13 July 2019|access-date=30 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.hamilton-victorious-as-verstappen-and-vettel-collide-in-silverstone.3yHjP4nXKPkt4HYJQ7Bagt.html|work=Formula 1|date=14 July 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|title=Hamilton victorious as Verstappen and Vettel collide in Silverstone thriller}}</ref> He crashed out from fourth place in the closing laps of the {{F1 GP|2019|German}},<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/motorsport/formula-one/valtteri-bottas-under-pressure-to-retain-mercedes-f1-seat-after-costly-error-in-chaotic-german-grand-prix/news-story/15fd022541b5f674d83501a809779c84|date=1 August 2019|title=Valtteri Bottas under pressure to retain Mercedes F1 seat after costly error in chaotic German Grand Prix|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Fox Sports Australia|last=Pavey|first=James}}</ref> and front-wing damage from contact with Leclerc resulted in an eighth-place finish at the {{F1 GP|2019|Hungarian}} whilst Hamilton claimed victory, leaving Bottas 62 points behind in the championship ahead of the summer break.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.2019-hungarian-grand-prix-bit-of-a-mess-bottas.1FBrfdkuIbFaG53MoaDUi2.html|date=4 August 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|title=Hungarian Grand Prix 'a bit of a mess' – Bottas|work=Formula 1}}</ref>

Further podiums came at the [[2019 Belgian Grand Prix|Belgian]], [[2019 Italian Grand Prix|Italian]] (where he finished less than a second behind winner Leclerc) and [[2019 Russian Grand Prix|Russian]] Grands Prix before he claimed his sixth Formula One victory at the {{F1 GP|2019|Japanese}}, having started the race behind both Ferraris. This result helped Mercedes clinch their sixth consecutive World Constructors' Championship.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/oct/13/formula-one-japanese-grand-prix-valtteri-bottas-mercedes-constructors-championship|last=Richards|first=Giles|work=The Guardian|date=13 October 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|title=Valtteri Bottas storms to win in Japan as Mercedes take F1 constructors' title}}</ref> He crashed heavily in qualifying at the {{F1 GP|2019|Mexican}} and started sixth, but recovered to third place in the race.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.watch-bottas-suffers-heavy-crash-at-the-end-of-qualifying.1ljZMi4IT4DdvUBT0Zvvj0.html|title=Bottas given all-clear after 'decent hit' into barriers in qualifying|date=26 October 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Formula 1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.mexican-grand-prix-2019-report-and-highlights.2GCUEuCYRquG0pcZeGZuYz.html|title=Hamilton closes in on title with supreme Mexico victory|date=27 October 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Formula 1}}</ref> He claimed victory from pole at the {{F1 GP|2019|United States}}, however this was insufficient to prevent race runner-up Hamilton from mathematically securing the championship with two races remaining.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.eurosport.com/formula-1/united-states-grand-prix/2019/us-gp-live-can-lewis-hamilton-win-a-sixth-title_sto7522949/story.shtml|date=4 November 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Eurosport|title=FORMULA ONE NEWS - LEWIS HAMILTON WINS CHAMPIONSHIP AT US GRAND PRIX|last=Ruthven|first=Graham}}</ref> Bottas retired from fifth place with an engine failure at the {{F1 GP|2019|Brazilian}} and ended the season with a fourth-place finish at the {{F1 GP|2019|Abu Dhabi}} after starting from the back of the grid.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.it-would-have-been-nice-to-be-involved-bottas-on-brazilian-gp-dnf.1kw6n4ExPzybnze9d3Golo.html|date=19 November 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Formula 1|title='It would have been nice to be involved' – Bottas on Brazilian GP DNF}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/11875472/abu-dhabi-gp-lewis-hamilton-signs-off-from-f1-2019-with-win|date=1 December 2019|access-date=30 May 2023|last=Galloway|first=James|work=Sky Sports|title=Abu Dhabi GP: Lewis Hamilton signs off from F1 2019 with win}}</ref>

Bottas finished the season in second place in the World Drivers' Championship with 326 points to Hamilton's 413. He recorded four wins, fifteen podium finishes, five pole positions and three fastest laps, making 2019 his most successful year at Mercedes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2019/drivers.html|work=Formula 1|title=2019 Driver Standings|access-date=30 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2019/drivers/VALBOT01/valtteri-bottas.html|work=Formula 1|access-date=30 May 2023|title=2019 Driver Standings: Valtteri Bottas}}</ref> He was rated the fourth-best driver of the season in a poll of the Formula One team principals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/revealed-f1s-team-bosses-choose-their-top-10-drivers-of-2019.3TENpziJ3cwIN9HBRBNv4Q|title=REVEALED: F1's team bosses choose their Top 10 drivers of 2019|website=formula1.com|first=Lawrence|last=Barretto|date=12 December 2019|accessdate=13 April 2024}}</ref> On his season, Bottas commented "I've not been able to be at my very, very best every single race, but much more often than ever before", and praised Hamilton's consistency.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/28026874/where-did-2019-go-wrong-valtteri-bottas|title=Where did 2019 go wrong for Valtteri Bottas?|website=espn.co.uk|first=Laurence|last=Edmondson|date=7 November 2019|accessdate=13 April 2024}}</ref>

Mercedes for 2020 F1 season alongside Lewis Hamilton|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.mercedes-retain-bottas-alongside-hamilton.LSNMCDW5zVT4brPY4pOEY.html|website=Formula1 news|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/11937751/f1-testing-day-one-am-valtteri-bottas-ahead-as-2020-starts-fast|location=Barcelona|first=Matt|last=Morlidge|work=Sky Sports|title=F1 Testing, from start to finish.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.planetf1.com/news/qualifying-report-austria-2020/|title=Qualy: Valtteri Bottas spins off but still takes pole|date=4 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite |access-date=14 July 2020}}</ref> Bottas qualified second behind Hamilton at the {{F1 GP|2020|Hungarian}}, but made a false start and lost four places at the first corner. He ran closely behind Hamilton for most of the race but fell back in the closing laps before suffering a tyre failure with four laps remaining. He returned to the pits for a tyre change and eventually finished 11th.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/articles/single-seaters/f1/2020-british-grand-prix-race-report-hamilton-holds-on-after-final-lap-blowout|title=2020 British Grand Prix race report: Hamilton holds on after final lap blowout|website=Motorsport Magazine |first=Chris|last=Medland|date=2 August 2020|access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref> Bottas secured pole position at the following week's [[70th Anniversary Grand Prix]] but dropped behind Hamilton in the race, and tyre issues for the Mercedes cars allowed Max Verstappen to pass both drivers to win. Bottas qualified second for the {{F1 GP|2020|Spanish}} but lost positions at the start and finished third behind Verstappen,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.dominant-hamilton-eases-to-fifth-spanish-gp-win-as-verstappen-splits.7rpPdVJJW3PHkrnNAisQ3G.html|date=16 August 2020|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Formula 1|title=Dominant Hamilton eases to fifth Spanish GP win as Verstappen splits Mercedes}}</ref> later commenting that the championship was "drifting away".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/world-championship-drifting-away-bottas/4858521/|title=Bottas admits championship now "drifting away"|website=motorsport.com|first=Adam|last=Cooper|date=16 August 2020|accessdate=30 May 2024}}</ref> He qualified and finished second at the {{F1 GP|2020|Belgian}},<ref>{{Cite news|date=30 August 2020|access-date=30 May 2023|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.hamilton-takes-masterful-fourth-win-at-spa-from-bottas-as-ferrari-finish-out.E8KCVXQHm4h6OdGoZHySe.html|work=Formula 1|title=Hamilton takes masterful fourth win at Spa from Bottas as Ferrari finish out of the points}}</ref> and again qualified second for the {{F1 GP|2020|Italian}}, but dropped places in the opening laps and finished fifth. Verstappen's retirement in the race allowed him to regain second place in the Drivers' Championship, 47 points behind Hamilton.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.bottas-baffled-by-poor-italian-gp-start-and-phantom-puncture-which-saw-him.Y1SkRYbdMMDSodBiyGdfw.html|title=Bottas baffled by poor Italian GP start and 'phantom puncture' which saw him drop down order|date=7 September 2020|access-date=30 May 2023|work=Formula 1}}</ref> At the {{F1 GP|2020|Tuscan}}, Bottas took the lead from pole-sitter Hamilton on the first lap. The race was [[Racing flags#red flag|red-flagged]] on lap seven after a multi-car accident, and Bottas lost the lead to Hamilton shortly after the restart and finished second.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.hamilton-beats-bottas-to-win-crazy-tuscan-gp-as-albon-secures-maiden-podium.6TqXlnjsxf0fZ5q0tubg18.html|date=13 September 2020|access-date=30 May 2023|title=Hamilton beats Bottas to win crazy Tuscan GP, as Albon secures maiden podium|work=Formula 1}}</ref> He qualified third behind Hamilton and Verstappen for the {{F1 GP|2020|Russian}}, but benefited from penalties issued to Hamilton to claim the ninth Grand Prix victory of his career.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2020/sep/27/formula-one-russian-grand-prix-race-report-valtteri-bottas-lewis-hamilton|last=Richards|first=Giles|work=The Guardian|title=Valtteri Bottas wins Russian GP as time penalty denies Hamilton's record bid|date=28 September 2020|access-date=30 May 2023}}</ref> Bottas took pole position for the {{F1 GP|2020|Eifel}} but was overtaken by Hamilton after a mistake on lap 13. He later retired from third place with power loss,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.hamilton-takes-record-equalling-91st-victory-at-eifel-gp-as-ricciardo-claims.5z1UB37DlpHwKWM9GBM90M.html|title=Hamilton takes record-equalling 91st victory as Ricciardo claims first Renault podium at Eifel GP|website=Formula1.com|date=11 October 2020|access-date=17 January 2022}}</ref> extending Hamilton's championship lead to 69 points.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/12102552/eifel-gp-f1-driver-ratings-the-grid-reviewed-and-rated|date=13 October 2020|access-date=30 May 2023|title=Eifel GP F1 driver ratings: The grid reviewed and rated|work=Sky Sports|last1=Morlidge|first1=Matt|last2=Galloway|first2=James}}</ref> Bottas finished second at both the [[2020 Portuguese Grand Prix|Portuguese]] and [[2020 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix|Emilia Romagna]] Grands Prix. the finish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/we-need-to-make-sure-it-doesnt-happen-again-bottas-reflects-on-52-second-pit.4hMNECVKLfPDeLZ0QhdhAE|title='We need to make Bottas was eliminated in Q1 at the following four races. Bottas described the race as the team's weakest of the year and remarked that the team's issues were "long-term".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-has-long-term-concern-over-sauber-struggles-after-weakest-race-of-f1-season/10648256/|title=Bottas has "long-term" concerns over Sauber struggles after "weakest" F1 race|website=motorsport.com|first1=Ewan|last1=Gale|first2=Jonathan|last2=Noble|date=27 August 2024|accessdate=14 April 2025}}</ref>

Bottas went into the season without a contract for {{F1|2025}}, but revealed early in the year that he had begun talks with [[Audi in Formula One|Audi]] ahead of their takeover of the Sauber team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-getting-ball-rolling-f1-future-talks/10594093/|title=Bottas "slowly getting the ball rolling" on F1 future talks|website=motorsport.com|date=3 April 2024|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref> In April it was announced that the team had signed [[Nico Hülkenberg]] for 2025, after which Bottas commented that he was "confident" of finding a seat, but that he could not afford to wait too long for Audi to decide on a second driver with his options narrowing at other teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-confident-not-to-miss-the-cut-for-f1-2025-spot/10624240/|title=Bottas "confident" not to miss the cutoff for F1 2025 spot|website=motorsport.com|first1=Filip|last1=Cleeren|first2=Jake|last2=Boxall-Legge|date=17 June 2024|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref> The second seat was ultimately taken by [[FIA Formula 2 Championship|Formula 2]] graduate [[Gabriel Bortoleto]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kick Sauber confirm rookie Bortoleto as second driver for 2025|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/breaking-kick-sauber-confirm-rookie-bortoleto-as-second-driver-for-2025.2EL5ciR1wh3baHcobZqGl9 |date=6 November 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Sauber's performance improved in the final races of the year; Bottas qualified 11th at the {{F1 GP|2024|São Paulo}}, finished 11th at the {{F1 GP|2024|Qatar}} with teammate Zhou scoring the team's only points of the season in eighth place,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/zhou-opens-up-on-relief-of-scoring-kick-saubers-first-points-of-2024-in.6QhBeJlDnCzjZPPtHBOQ6L |title=Zhou opens up on 'relief' of scoring Kick Sauber's first points of 2024 in Qatar after 'draining season'|website=Formula 1.com|date=1 December 2024|accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> and reached Q3 at the {{F1 GP|2024|Abu Dhabi}}, but went on to retire with collision damage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/what-the-teams-said-race-day-in-abu-dhabi-2024.7yQ4yr2n6uWcheAYJmGZy3|title=What the teams said – Race day in Abu Dhabi|website=Formula 1.com|date=8 December 2024|accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> Bottas described the improvements as "ironic" given his imminent departure from the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-its-ironic-that-sauber-f1-improvement-has-come-so-late/10678209/|title=Bottas: It's "ironic" that Sauber F1 improvement has come so late|website=motorsport.com|first=Stuart|last=Codling|date=1 December 2024|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref> 

Bottas ended the season 22nd in the World Drivers' Championship, last of the full-time drivers, and failed to score points over a season for the first time in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.planetf1.com/news/f1-results-2024-abu-dhabi-grand-prix-race-standings |title=2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix – F1 race results and final standings for F1 2024 season |last=Valantine |first=Henry |date=8 December 2024 |website=PlanetF1.com |access-date=9 December 2024}}</ref> Reflecting on his three-year tenure at the team, he described his move there in 2022 as a "mistake" and that it was "downhill" after the first year. He also revealed that his decision to join the team was influenced by the presence of team principal [[Frédéric Vasseur]] and that he considered exercising an option to leave the team when Vasseur moved to Ferrari, but was convinced to stay after being told he would be a "pillar" of the Audi project.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/former-f1-race-winner-bottas-labels-his-sauber-career-a-mistake-after-difficult-2024/10680852/|title=F1 race winner Bottas labels his Sauber career "a mistake" after difficult 2024|website=motorsport.com|first=Anthony|last=Wood|date=9 December 2024|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref>

===Mercedes reserve driver (2025)===
In December 2024, it was announced that Bottas would be re-joining Mercedes as a reserve driver for {{F1|2025}}.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/bottas-rejoins-mercedes-as-2025-f1-reserve-driver/10683607/ | title=Bottas rejoins Mercedes as 2025 F1 reserve driver }}</ref> He described the move as "like coming back home" and stated his goal was to return to a full-time seat in {{F1|2026}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/valtteri-bottas-on-future/10702442/|title=Valtteri Bottas targets 2026 F1 comeback as he outlines Mercedes role|website=motorsport.com|first=Lydia|last=Mee|date=13 March 2025|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref> He revealed that he was offered a seat in the [[IndyCar Series]], but chose to reject the offer due to his concerns about struggling to adapt to a new category after twelve years in Formula One.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/bottas-reveals-indycar-switch-offer-as-indy-500-piques-interest-/10677205/|title=Bottas reveals IndyCar switch offer as Indy 500 piques interest|website=motorsport.com|first=Ewan|last=Gale|date=28 November 2024|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref> In March, he undertook a private test in the [[McLaren MCL60]] as part of a reserve driver sharing arrangement between Mercedes and McLaren.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/why-bottas-has-been-driving-for-mclaren/|title=Why Bottas has been driving for McLaren|website=the-race.com|first=Jack|last=Cozens|date=28 March 2025|accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref>

===Philanthropy===
In 2017, Bottas launched the ''Valtteri Bottas Duathlon'', an annual sporting event held in Finland, which raises money for charity.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Valtteri Bottas Duathlon powered by Tunturi|url=https://www.valtteribottasduathlon.com/en/|access-date=13 January 2021|website=Valtteri Bottas Duathlon|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=22 August 2017|title=Valtteri Bottas runs for the Starlight Children's Foundation|url=https://f1i.com/images/277141-bottas-runs-starlight-childrens-foundation.html|access-date=13 January 2021|website=F1i.com|language=en}}</ref> In May 2022, in collaboration with German photographer [[Paul Ripke]], more than 5,000 print copies were sold of a photo taken by Cromwell of Bottas naked in an [[Aspen, Colorado]] stream, raising more than €50,000 for charity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/f1-winner-bottas-surprised-by-weird-50k-success-from-bum-picture/10310250/|title=F1 winner Bottas surprised by 'weird' €50k success from bum picture|website=autosport.com|first1=Luke|last1=Smith|first2=Oleg|last2=Karpov|date=25 May 2022|accessdate=1 June 2024}}</ref> Bottas again worked with Ripke in 2023 to create a [[nude calendar]], titled ''BOTTASS 2024'', which raised [[US Dollar|$]]150,000 for [[men's health]] organisation [[Movember]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/naked-bottas-calendar-raises-150000-for-charity-despite-his-mums-concerns/10553776/|title=Naked Bottas calendar raises $150,000 for charity despite his mum's concerns|website=motorsport.com|first=Adam|last=Cooper|date=30 November 2023|accessdate=1 June 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On 11 September 2016, Bottas married his long-time girlfriend, [[Emilia Pikkarainen]], a fellow Finn and an Olympic swimmer whom he had been dating since 2010. The couple were married at [[St. John's Church, Helsinki|St. John's Church]] in [[Helsinki]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thisisf1.com/2016/09/12/valtteri-bottas-gets-married-in-helsinki/|title=Valtteri Bottas gets married in Helsinki|date=12 September 2016|work=thisisf1.com|access-date=16 October 2016}}</ref> On 28 November 2019, Bottas announced their separation and divorce, citing the "challenges my career and life situation bring".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/B5Z94AziFBZ/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/B5Z94AziFBZ |archive-date=23 December 2021 |url-access=subscription|title=Valtteri Bottas on Instagram: "Unfortunately I have to share you the news that the marriage between Emilia and myself has come to an end. Our ways have split because of…"|via=Instagram|language=en|access-date=28 November 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Since February 2020, Bottas has been in a relationship with Australian cyclist [[Tiffany Cromwell]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Medland|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.punk-rock-and-pizzas-getting-to-know-the-real-valtteri-bottas.46gSAuC9ASQrZ2rIuL1hmZ.html|title=Punk rock and pizzas – Getting to know the real Valtteri Bottas|work=Formula1.com|publisher=Formula One World Championship Limited|date=27 September 2020|access-date=6 December 2020|quote=Not just because my girlfriend Tiffany Cromwell is from Stirling, South Australia!}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.is.fi/olympialaiset/art-2000008147868.html|title=Valtteri Bottas odottaa jo olympiasunnuntaita – tyttöystävä pääsee irti Tokion maantiepyöräilyssä: "Iso päivä!"|language=Finnish|trans-title=Valtteri Bottas is already looking forward to Olympic Sunday – girlfriend gets out on a road bike ride in Tokyo: "Big day!"|work=[[Ilta-Sanomat]]|publisher=[[Sanoma]]|date=24 July 2021|accessdate=24 July 2021}}</ref> Bottas has residences in [[McLaren Vale|McLaren Vale, South Australia]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://glamadelaide.com.au/formula-1-superstar-valtteri-bottas-and-cyclist-tiffany-cromwell-put-down-permanent-roots-in-sa/ |title=Formula 1 superstar Valtteri Bottas and cyclist Tiffany Cromwell put down permanent roots in SA |website=glamadelaide.com.au |date=14 November 2025 |first=Bella |last=McGreevy |access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref> and Monaco, and also has a lake house in his native Finland.<ref name="Charlton 2021">{{cite web | last=Charlton | first=Alistair | title=Lake Houses, Coffee And Life Beyond Formula One: An Interview With Valtteri Bottas | website=Forbes | date=4 August 2021 | url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alistaircharlton/2021/08/04/lake-houses-coffee-and-life-beyond-formula-one-an-interview-with-valtteri-bottas/ | access-date=20 December 2021}}</ref>
